explanation: Newton's first law says an object keeps its velocity unless a net force acts on it. Set friction mu = 0 and the puck glides forever at the same speed (green velocity arrow never shrinks) because the net force is zero. Add friction and a backward net force (red arrow) appears, decelerating the puck at a = mu*g until it stops — proving that a CHANGE in motion always needs a net force.
bullets: With zero net force, velocity stays constant — speed and direction unchanged.
Friction is the net force here; it decelerates the puck at a = mu*g.
Inertia is the tendency to resist any change in motion.
